verdict: Old Dominion grew revenue 13% to $1.6B on higher pricing per hundredweight, and its operating ratio improved to 71.5%, lifting profit 27%.

kpis.label: Operating ratio
kpis.note: vs 74.3% a year ago — lower is better

segments.name: LTL services
segments.note: Less-than-truckload freight — almost all revenue, up 13% on pricing, with tons per day roughly flat.

segments.name: Other services
segments.note: Other services such as drayage, brokerage and consulting — up 16%.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Trucks, trailers and service centers wearing out — a non-cash cost.

otherDetail: Other is net non-operating income of about $2M: $4M of interest income, less $2M of other expense and negligible interest expense. Figures are rounded to $M from the release's thousands, so operating income is shown as $453M vs the reported $452.6M.
footerNote: For this trucking report, direct operating costs in cost of revenue are salaries, wages and benefits ($705M), operating supplies and expenses ($189M) and purchased transportation ($35M); the remaining operating expense lines are shown as operating expenses. Amounts are rounded to $M.

takeaways.title: Pricing drove growth
takeaways.text: LTL revenue per hundredweight rose 13.3% while LTL tons per day fell 0.1% — growth was price, not volume.

takeaways.title: Operating ratio improved
takeaways.text: Operating expenses were 71.5% of revenue, down from 74.3% — salaries and overhead both leveraged the revenue gain.

takeaways.title: EPS up 29%
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS rose to $1.65 from $1.28, on net income of $344M.
